bull.b: Sustained clinical improvements through 12 months, alongside reduced reliance on chronic immunotherapies, support miv-cel’s potential durability. If confirmed in regulatory review, this profile could differentiate the therapy and strengthen its prospects in severe autoimmune disease.

Low leverage reduces refinancing pressure and preserves greater financial flexibility than a highly indebted clinical-stage biotech. This gives Kyverna more capacity to direct available capital toward trials, manufacturing development and regulatory work while advancing miv-cel.

Positive follow-up across stiff person syndrome and generalized myasthenia gravis supports the potential breadth of Kyverna’s autoimmune CAR T approach. Demonstrated activity in multiple diseases may create a platform opportunity beyond a single indication if later-stage studies confirm these results.

bear.b: The absence of commercial revenue leaves Kyverna dependent on clinical execution and future financing rather than internally generated sales. Until a therapy is approved and launched, the company has limited operating leverage and little revenue visibility to offset its development costs.

Heavy and persistent cash consumption increases the funding required to complete trials, manufacturing development and regulatory activities. Deteriorating free cash flow can shorten financial runway and make future capital raises increasingly important before products generate revenue.

Widening losses and a shrinking equity base indicate that ongoing operations are consuming shareholder capital without current commercial support. This weakens financial resilience over time and may constrain Kyverna’s ability to fund its pipeline without additional equity issuance.
